purpose: Measurement limit of the clock used by every CF5 harness, fixed before the campaign (plan section 6.1). Instrument calibration only: no cluster-forest observation is used.
clock: std::time::Instant in every analyzed harness (knotrel-benchmarks, cf5-core, release-cells, http-lifecycle, contention-probe; v1.0.0 harness df635a1e: same replay loop)

measured.tick_ns: back-to-back deltas take only the values 0, 41, 42, 83, 84, 125 ns (10^7 deltas x 5 runs): a 24 MHz counter, tick 41.667 ns
measured.clock_read_ns: Instant::now() 13.92-14.14 ns per call; empty timed interval mean 14.25-14.52 ns; summed per-operation timing exceeds one aggregate interval by 14.94-15.08 ns per operation (clock-runs.txt)
measured.serialization: per-operation timing also stops overlap between consecutive operations: for a 42-56 ns operation the summed per-operation time exceeds the aggregate by 63-77 ns per operation (clock-runs.txt, spin(100)). Operation-dependent, not an additive constant; not part of the limit below (stated limitation, plan section 6.1)
measured.harness_gap_ns_per_op: workload_wall_ns minus the sum of per-operation intervals, divided by the timed operations, compact-bfs, 5 repetitions per workload, two runs (harness-gap-run1.txt, harness-gap-run2.txt): knotrel-benchmarks (candidate) 18.8-33.2, A harness candidate 19.1-25.8, A harness v1.0.0 18.6-24.4

constants.rounding: each constant is the ceiling, in whole ns, of the largest value observed (tick: exact)

workload_operations.source: timed operations per K1/V2/V3 workload at the CF5 rounds (100; 20 for sustained), identical at every size (harness-gap runs)

l3_churn_operations.source: release-cells churn 'operations' (deterministic per argv; equality checked per pair by same_trace)
